project-brief.text:
{
  "issue": 21,
  "product": "Tabs is a shared-expense web app for friends, flatmates, couples and trips: people sign up, create a group, share a join link, record who paid what and how it splits, see what each member owes or is owed, and settle up in the fewest payments. It is a Node HTTP application over a managed Postgres, with the domain logic (integer minor-unit money, exact splits, minimal-transfer settlement) kept as pure modules that never touch the network or the database, and a static ES-module frontend served by the same process. What already exists — exact paise arithmetic, the greedy settlement, a JSON API with a typed error envelope — is kept and moved onto a real database behind real accounts; what does not exist yet — persistence that survives a redeploy, identities, and permissions on every group read and write — is built in that order, because a group a stranger can change is not a product anyone trusts with money.",
  "stack": {
    "choice": "Node.js 22+ (Vercel default 24.x) with node:http and no web framework; the existing `src/server.js` stays the entrypoint and calls `server.listen()` at module scope, which is the shape Vercel captures as a Node server. Managed Postgres (Neon today; any Postgres host works) reached through the single runtime dependency `pg`, with a small client pool over the host's pooled endpoint and plain SQL migrations in `migrations/*.sql` applied by `bin/migrate.js`. No build step, no bundler, no ORM, no framework, no TypeScript, no edge runtime. Passwords hashed with `node:crypto` scrypt; sessions are opaque random tokens in an http-only cookie, stored server-side as a hash. Frontend is native ES modules served statically from `public/` — no client framework. Tests are `node:test`.",
    "why": "The spec's hard constraint is Vercel plus a managed database, and Vercel's own Node runtime documentation says it looks for a `server.js` / `src/server.js` entrypoint that calls `listen()` during module startup and routes requests to it. That is the file this repository already has, so the hosting constraint the spec introduces costs this project no framework and no build step. The domain risk in Tabs has never been infrastructure — it is money arithmetic and settlement — so the thing worth protecting is that `src/money.js` and `src/domain.js` stay pure and testable with no database, and that the database lives behind `src/repo/*` where the SQL is. One runtime dependency (`pg`) is the whole cost of persistence; an ORM would add a schema layer, a client-generation step and a migration dialect to a data model of nine tables. A static ES-module frontend keeps `sdlc:serve` a single `node src/server.js` and keeps the pipeline's browser driving deterministic, at the cost of hand-written DOM, which is a few lines per screen and no build to break. scrypt from the standard library is OWASP's second-choice password KDF and the only one available without a native module, which matters on a serverless runtime where a native addon is a deployment risk.",
    "rejected": [
      {
        "option": "Next.js / React Router / any Vercel-blessed full-stack framework",
        "because": "It brings a bundler, a build step and a client framework into `sdlc:verify` and `sdlc:serve`, and it replaces the pure domain modules with server-component boundaries. Everything it buys is rendering machinery this five-screen product does not need, and everything it costs lands in the pipeline that has to boot the app on every QA run."
      },
      {
        "option": "Prisma or Drizzle as the data layer",
        "because": "Codegen or a migration dialect, a generated client in the repository, and schema changes that are only expressible in the ORM's vocabulary. Nine tables and hand-written SQL keep every query visible, keep the domain tests database-free, and remove a class of build failure from CI."
      },
      {
        "option": "@neondatabase/serverless (the HTTP/WebSocket driver)",
        "because": "Neon's own current guidance for Vercel with Fluid compute is a standard TCP `pg.Pool`; the HTTP driver is the fallback for edge runtimes where TCP is unavailable, and this app runs on the Node runtime. It would also add a second, less familiar driver to debug."
      },
      {
        "option": "Turso / libSQL, SQLite on Vercel, or any hosted KV as the store",
        "because": "The spec asks for migrations applied on deploy and every read and write checked against group members, which is a relational job: memberships, ledgers and a feed are joins. A KV store would push that into application code that the pipeline then has to test."
      },
      {
        "option": "A client framework (React, Vue, Svelte) for the frontend",
        "because": "It adds a build step to a pipeline whose `sdlc:serve` is currently one Node process, and it replaces a 25KB static page with a bundle whose size and boot behaviour QA would have to re-verify on every ticket."
      },
      {
        "option": "argon2id via a native module (@node-rs/argon2 or argon2)",
        "because": "It is OWASP's first choice, so this is a real trade and not a dismissal: a prebuilt native addon on a serverless runtime is a deployment risk, it needs a `postinstall` or a rebuild step that ci-verify deliberately runs with `--ignore-scripts`, and it is a second runtime dependency for a KDF the standard library already provides. Revisit if the maintainer decides the OWASP ordering outranks the deployment risk."
      },
      {
        "option": "Keeping the JSON file store and adding accounts on top of it",
        "because": "The spec's first hard constraint rules it out: the Vercel function filesystem is read-only apart from /tmp, and a cold start or a redeploy takes the data with it. It is also the reason issue 21 exists."
      }
    ]
  },
  "architecture": {
    "shape": "One Node HTTP server process. `src/server.js` is the entrypoint: it creates the node:http server and calls `listen()` at module scope, which is both what Vercel captures and what `npm run sdlc:serve` runs locally — the same file, one code path. Everything in the request goes router -> auth (resolve the session cookie to a user id) -> handler -> `src/repo/*` (SQL, always filtered by membership) -> `src/domain.js` and `src/money.js` (pure validation, split arithmetic, balances, settlement) -> Postgres; the response is JSON, or a static file from `public/`, or the SPA shell for a client route. The boundaries are: HTTP lives in `src/app.js` and never contains SQL or business rules; SQL lives in `src/repo/*` and never contains business rules or HTTP; the domain modules are pure and import neither. The frontend is native ES modules talking to `/api/*` over fetch with the session cookie, with no build step between `public/` and the browser.",
    "modules": [
      { "path": "src/server.js", "holds": "The Vercel entrypoint: creates the node:http server and calls listen() at module scope, so the same file boots locally and in production." },
      { "path": "src/app.js", "holds": "The request handler: route matching, body and cookie parsing, session resolution, the error envelope. No SQL, no business rules." },
      { "path": "src/db.js", "holds": "The only module that speaks to Postgres: pool lifecycle, query helper, transaction helper, and the boot check that names a missing DATABASE_URL." },
      { "path": "src/auth.js", "holds": "Password hashing with scrypt, session token issue/verify/expire, and the sign-in rate limit." },
      { "path": "src/repo/users.js", "holds": "SQL for accounts, profiles, sessions, login attempts and password-reset tokens." },
      { "path": "src/repo/groups.js", "holds": "SQL for groups, memberships, placeholder claims, invites and the actor-scoped group list." },
      { "path": "src/repo/expenses.js", "holds": "SQL for expenses, their payers and their split entries, scoped to the actor's membership." },
      { "path": "src/repo/payments.js", "holds": "SQL for settle-up payments, the activity feed, and the cross-group balance rollup." },
      { "path": "src/money.js", "holds": "Integer minor-unit arithmetic and the four split algorithms, each distributing the remainder so the parts sum to the whole. Pure, no I/O." },
      { "path": "src/domain.js", "holds": "The model and the rules: validating expenses and splits, deriving per-member balances, and the deterministic minimal-transfer settlement. Pure, no I/O." },
      { "path": "migrations/", "holds": "Append-only numbered .sql files, applied in order by bin/migrate.js and recorded in schema_migrations. An applied migration is never edited." },
      { "path": "bin/migrate.js", "holds": "The migration runner: applies pending migrations one transaction each, for local use, for CI and on deploy." },
      { "path": "bin/seed.js", "holds": "QA and development fixtures: truncates and rebuilds a group with expenses of every split type, payments and a placeholder member." },
      { "path": "bin/migrate-legacy.js", "holds": "One-time import of data/groups.json into Postgres as a group owned by one imported account, keeping every member, expense and settlement." },
      { "path": "public/", "holds": "The frontend: index.html shell, styles.css carrying the design tokens, and native ES modules for the router, the API client and one module per screen." },
      { "path": "test/", "holds": "node:test suites: pure-domain tests that need no database, and HTTP and repository tests that run only when TEST_DATABASE_URL is set." }
    ]
  },
  "invariants": [
    "An amount is an integer count of its group's currency minor unit, everywhere inside the system. No float ever touches an amount: input is parsed to an integer at the boundary and output is formatted from an integer at the boundary, and the display exponent comes from the currency, never a hard-coded 100.",
    "The parts of a split always sum to exactly the whole, and the rounding remainder goes to the stated member. No split is ever rounded per share; if a split cannot be made to sum exactly, it is refused with an error naming the discrepancy and by how much.",
    "Balances are derived from an append-only ledger of expenses and payments and are never mutated in place. A group's balances always net to zero; if they do not, the request fails loudly with BALANCES_INVARIANT and a failing test rather than being papered over.",
    "Every read and write of a group's data is authorized against that actor's membership in the same statement that fetches or changes the row. A repository function that touches group data takes the actor id as an argument; there is no path that mutates a group without one, and no anonymous mutation anywhere.",
    "Identity comes only from the server-side session record. A user id, group id or member id in a request body is a claim to be checked, never an authority, and a session token's cookie is http-only and SameSite=Lax so client script cannot read it.",
    "`src/server.js` calls `server.listen()` at module scope and no request path writes to local disk. The Vercel function filesystem is read-only apart from /tmp and is thrown away on a cold start, so anything a user saves is in Postgres or it is lost."
  ],
  "conventions": [
    "ES modules only, Node 22+, no build step and no bundler. `\"type\": \"module\"` stays; files are named as they are today.",
    "`pg` is the only runtime dependency. Adding a second one is an architecture-level change recorded as a decision in this brief, not a ticket-level choice.",
    "`src/money.js` and `src/domain.js` stay pure: they import nothing from db.js, auth.js, the repos or node:http, and no test that covers them needs a database.",
    "Every SQL statement lives in `src/repo/*`, is written with placeholders ($1, $2, ...) and never interpolates a value into the query text.",
    "A repository function that reads or writes group data takes `actorId` as its first argument and filters on membership in the same statement, so an authorization bug cannot be introduced by forgetting a check in the handler.",
    "Money columns are BIGINT of minor units; a group carries its own currency code. No REAL, FLOAT or NUMERIC money column, ever.",
    "Migrations are append-only: a new `migrations/NNNN_name.sql`, applied inside a transaction and recorded in `schema_migrations`. An already-applied migration is never edited — a correction is a new migration.",
    "Errors are thrown as the app's own classes carrying a `code` and an HTTP status; the wire shape stays `{ error: { code, message } }`. A response never carries a stack trace, SQL text or a Postgres error string.",
    "The write path reads state after it has awaited the body: any handler that reads, modifies and writes must do its reads after `await parseBody(req)`, which is the concurrency bug this repository has already shipped once.",
    "Sessions are an opaque random token in an http-only, SameSite=Lax, Secure cookie; the database stores only the token's hash, and signing out deletes the row server-side rather than asking the browser to forget.",
    "Tests are `node:test` and `node:assert`. Pure-logic tests need no database; any test that touches the database skips with a printed reason when `TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset, so CI stays green without a database and nobody mistakes a skip for coverage.",
    "The frontend sets user data with `textContent` and never `innerHTML`; the existing XSS suite keeps passing against the rewritten screens.",
    "Commit subjects are Conventional Commits, and the body states what changed, why, and how it was verified."
  ],
  "commands": {
    "verify": "node --test test/",
    "serve": "node src/server.js",
    "seed": "node bin/seed.js",
    "ready": "curl -fsS http://localhost:3000/health"
  },
  "deploy": "Production and previews run on Vercel, connected to this repository through the Git integration: every pull request gets a preview URL automatically, and merge to main produces the production deployment. `src/server.js` is the deployment unit — Vercel's Node runtime looks for that entrypoint and routes requests to the server it listens on — so there is no build command, no output directory and no framework preset to choose beyond Other. Both are created by a person, not by an agent: the owner adds the Vercel project, connects Shivam-Fl/tabs-v2, adds the Neon (or other Postgres) integration, and sets `DATABASE_URL` (pooled, for the app) and `DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED` (for migrations) as project and preview environment variables. Migrations run on deploy with `npm run migrate`; the alternative — a human running them before promoting — is a step somebody will eventually forget, and the spec asks for migrations applied on deploy. As `.sdlc/config.yml` stands, QA does not drive a Vercel preview: `env.mode: compose` boots `npm run sdlc:serve` on localhost:3000 inside the workflow runner with `url_allowlist: localhost:*`, against the `DATABASE_URL` QA workflow secret. That is deliberate and cheap — QA drives a fresh process every run, and the preview is for a human — but it means the preview deployment is not covered by the pipeline's own testing, and switching QA onto previews is a one-line config change (env.mode: preview plus the preview host in url_allowlist) whenever that is wanted. A preview database per pull request is available through the Neon integration and is not enabled by this brief: it is still framed as beta, and QA is not driving previews, so the branch-per-PR machinery would have no consumer. The honest gap: until a person creates the Vercel project, nothing is deployed, and `sdlc:verify`, `sdlc:serve` and QA all continue to work against a local process.",
  "decisions": [
    {
      "title": "Keep node:http and src/server.js; it is already the shape Vercel captures",
      "decision": "The server stays a plain node:http application, and `src/server.js` is refactored so it creates the server and calls `server.listen()` at module scope. No framework, no build step, and one code path for local QA and for production.",
      "because": "Vercel's Node runtime documentation says it looks for a `server.{js,mjs,ts}` or `src/server.{js,mjs,ts}` entrypoint, uses the `listen()` call made during module startup to detect the HTTP server, and routes incoming requests to it through an internal port. This repository already has that file with that shape; today it only listens when run directly, which is the one thing that has to change.",
      "consequences": "Easy: no framework to learn, version, or break, and QA boots the same entrypoint that production runs. Hard: routing, cookies, body parsing and static-file serving are hand-written, and a captured server receives raw IncomingMessage/ServerResponse with none of the `/api` handler helpers (`request.query`, `request.cookies`, `request.body`) — which is fine, because this server already parses them itself. Tests must stop importing the listening server and import a handler factory instead, or importing them in a test process will start listening as a side effect."
    },
    {
      "title": "Managed Postgres over the JSON file, with pg as the only runtime dependency",
      "decision": "Storage is a managed Postgres reached through `pg`, with hand-written SQL in `src/repo/*` and plain .sql migrations. There is no ORM, no codegen and no query builder.",
      "because": "The spec's hard constraints require persistence that survives a redeploy and a cold start, and schema changes as migrations. Nine tables of memberships, a ledger and a feed are relational work; doing it in SQL keeps the queries readable in a diff and keeps the domain modules testable with no database at all.",
      "consequences": "Easy: an agent reading a diff can see the exact SQL, the schema is a folder of .sql files, and the pure domain logic is untouched by the migration. Hard: every query is hand-written and must be parameterised, `node_modules` now exists, and repository tests need a real Postgres to be meaningful — which is why they skip cleanly when `TEST_DATABASE_URL` is absent."
    },
    {
      "title": "Vercel's own Postgres is gone; the host is Neon, but the code is host-agnostic",
      "decision": "Neon is the named host today, reached with a standard `pg.Pool` over Neon's pooled connection string, with the unpooled string reserved for migrations. Nothing in `src/db.js` is Neon-specific.",
      "because": "Vercel Postgres was retired and its databases moved to Neon; Neon is the first-party integration on the Vercel Marketplace, and its current guidance for Vercel with Fluid compute is a normal TCP `pg.Pool` rather than the HTTP serverless driver. Depending on a provider SDK would re-couple the code to a host that has already changed once.",
      "consequences": "Easy: changing hosts is a connection string and a migrations run. Hard: the pooled-endpoint-plus-small-client-pool arrangement is easy to get wrong — a client pool on a non-pooled endpoint exhausts connections under serverless concurrency — so the pool is kept at one connection per instance and the migration path is the only user of the direct endpoint."
    },
    {
      "title": "Passwords hashed with scrypt from node:crypto",
      "decision": "scrypt (N=2^15, r=8, p=3, an OWASP-published parameter set) with a per-password random salt, verified in constant time, and rehashed on next sign-in if the parameters change. No native password-hashing dependency.",
      "because": "OWASP ranks argon2id first and names scrypt as the choice when Argon2id is unavailable. In Node there is no built-in argon2id, and the usual libraries are native addons — on a serverless runtime that is a deployment risk, and ci-verify installs with `--ignore-scripts`, so an addon needing a build step would not even be built there.",
      "consequences": "Easy: no native build, no install script, one less dependency, and the hash is portable across any Node host. Hard: it is not OWASP's first choice, it costs roughly 100ms of CPU per verification (a login is a slow operation by design), and Node's scrypt defaults need `maxmem` raised above 32 MiB for this parameter set. The decision is reversible in one module if the maintainer later prefers argon2id."
    },
    {
      "title": "Opaque server-side sessions, not JWTs and not a session framework",
      "decision": "Sign-in issues 256 bits of randomness; the cookie carries the token, the database stores only its SHA-256, and signing out deletes the row. There is no signed token and no stateless verification.",
      "because": "Sign-out has to end the session on the server, and account deletion and the 'remove a member with a non-zero balance' rules both need the server to be able to stop honouring a session immediately. A JWT cannot do that without a blocklist, which is the session table wearing a hat.",
      "consequences": "Easy: sign-out, deletion and expiry are all one DELETE, and a stolen-token list is a query. Hard: every authenticated request costs one row lookup against Postgres, and sessions are a table to migrate and to expire."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sign-up needs no email verification, and password reset degrades to a page that says so",
      "decision": "A new account is usable the moment it is created; only password reset sends email, and only when an email provider key is configured. With no key, `/reset-password` says the feature is unavailable rather than failing.",
      "because": "The spec asks for reset 'when an email provider is configured' and says nothing about verification, and requiring verification would mean the pipeline's QA could never get past sign-up — a QA session that cannot log in reports infrastructure, not bugs. A dependency-free signup also keeps the only email integration optional.",
      "consequences": "Easy: QA signs itself up and drives everything, and the email provider is one environment variable and one fetch call. Hard: an unverified email address can be attached to a real account, so the app must not treat an address as proof of anything, and spam signup is possible — which is what the sign-in rate limit and a signup cap will eventually have to address."
    },
    {
      "title": "The frontend is native ES modules, split one file per screen",
      "decision": "`public/` becomes index.html, styles.css, and small ES modules: a router, an API client and one module per screen. No client framework, no bundler, no build step.",
      "because": "The current 25KB single file works for two views and will not work for the eight this spec adds — and the failure mode is operational, not aesthetic: every agent's branch edits the same file, so two tickets touching the UI conflict on every line. Splitting by screen keeps each ticket's diff to its own file and keeps `sdlc:serve` a single process.",
      "consequences": "Easy: no bundle, no build to break, a browser can be pointed at the served file, and the design tokens live in one stylesheet every screen must use. Hard: rendering is hand-written DOM, routing is a hand-written matcher, and there is no component system to lean on for consistency — which is exactly why this brief fixes the tokens, patterns and layouts once."
    },
    {
      "title": "Balances stay derived from an append-only ledger",
      "decision": "Expenses and payments are never updated in place where a change of meaning is involved; an edit records a new version, a delete tombstones the row, and balances are always recomputed by folding the ledger.",
      "because": "The activity feed has to say who changed what and when, and a payment that moves balances and can be deleted by the members involved only works if the history is the truth and the balance is a view over it.",
      "consequences": "Easy: the feed falls out of the same ledger, an undo is an insert, and a balance can always be explained. Hard: a group with a long ledger recomputes on every read, so the balance query needs an index and eventually a cached projection — a decision this brief defers until there is a group big enough to need one."
    },
    {
      "title": "The existing JSON groups are imported once, as placeholder members of one imported account",
      "decision": "`bin/migrate-legacy.js` reads `data/groups.json` and creates a single 'imported' account owning each group, with every existing member name kept as a placeholder member, so a later sign-up through the group's invite link claims that placeholder and inherits its history.",
      "because": "The issue asks how the existing groups, expenses and settlements move onto the new store. Inventing an account per named member would fabricate identities that never existed; placeholder members are already a concept the spec defines for exactly this — recorded before the person has an account.",
      "consequences": "Easy: no history is lost, no identity is invented, and the import reuses the claiming flow rather than adding a second one. Hard: the imported groups have one owner who is not any of the members, and there is no real user data to preserve in any case, so the import can be dropped by the owner without loss."
    },
    {
      "title": "SQLite is not an option and neither is any store that needs a disk",
      "decision": "No SQLite, no file-backed store, no in-memory cache that a request depends on. The only durable state is Postgres.",
      "because": "The spec's first hard constraint is a Vercel deployment with no local disk that outlives a request, and the current JSON store is exactly what issue 21 says cannot carry it.",
      "consequences": "Easy: local, CI and production behave the same way, and there is no second code path to keep honest. Hard: `node --test` can no longer cover the storage layer without a database, which is why repository tests are separated and skipped cleanly rather than silently passing against a fake."
    }
  ],
  "research": {
    "questions": [
      "Can the Node application this repository already has run on Vercel, or does the spec's hosting constraint force a framework rewrite?",
      "Which hosted Postgres is current on Vercel, given that Vercel Postgres was retired?",
      "With a Vercel-hosted function and a managed Postgres, is the right driver a normal TCP pool or a serverless HTTP/WebSocket driver?",
      "What password hash is both OWASP-acceptable and available in the Node standard library, so that no native addon has to be built on a serverless runtime?",
      "Which Node versions does Vercel run today, and is the version this repository targets still supported?",
      "What does the Vercel function filesystem permit, and does anything survive a cold start?",
      "Can a pull request get a database of its own, so a preview deployment is not sharing production data?"
    ],
    "findings": [
      {
        "claim": "Vercel runs this repository's existing server shape: it detects a `server.js` or `src/server.js` entrypoint that calls `server.listen()` during module startup and routes requests to that server through an internal port.",
        "evidence": "\"Use a Node.js server when you want one HTTP server to route requests for your application. Vercel detects a `server` entrypoint and turns it into a Vercel Function. Vercel looks for a `server` entrypoint in the project root or the `src/` directory: `server.{js,cjs,mjs,ts,cts,mts}`, `src/server.{js,cjs,mjs,ts,cts,mts}`. Call `server.listen()` during module startup. Vercel uses that call to detect the HTTP server, then routes incoming requests to the server through an internal port. The port you pass to `listen()` is only used when you run the file locally and does not expose a public port on Vercel.\" The same page notes: \"To use ES modules in JavaScript, name the file `server.mjs` or set `\"type\": \"module\"` in `package.json`.\" — this repository already sets `\"type\": \"module\"` and already has `src/server.js`.",
        "source": "https://vercel.com/docs/functions/runtimes/node-js (last_updated 2026-08-11)",
        "confidence": 93,
        "affects": "stack.choice, architecture.shape, the first ADR, TR-1"
      },
      {
        "claim": "A server captured this way gets raw Node request and response objects, so cookie parsing and body reading must be hand-written exactly as they are today.",
        "evidence": "\"Captured Node.js servers receive standard Node.js `IncomingMessage` and `ServerResponse` objects. They do not include the helper properties added to `/api` function handlers, such as `request.query`, `request.cookies`, and `request.body`.\" The helpers only apply to files in the `/api` directory, which this design does not use.",
        "source": "https://vercel.com/docs/functions/runtimes/node-js",
        "confidence": 92,
        "affects": "architecture.shape, conventions (cookies and body parsing stay hand-written), TR-6"
      },
      {
        "claim": "Vercel Postgres no longer exists; Neon is the replacement, so a brief written from memory about a Vercel database would be choosing something already retired.",
        "evidence": "Vercel's own page states \"Vercel Postgres is no longer available. If you had an existing Vercel Postgres database, we automatically moved it to Neon in December 2024.\" The Vercel changelog records Neon arriving on the Marketplace on 2024-11-15 as \"This integration replaces the existing Vercel Postgres.\"",
        "source": "https://vercel.com/docs/postgres and https://vercel.com/changelog/neon-now-available-on-vercel-marketplace",
        "confidence": 95,
        "affects": "stack.choice, the third ADR (host is Neon), the deploy section"
      },
      {
        "claim": "For a Node function on Vercel with Fluid compute, Neon currently recommends a standard TCP `pg.Pool` rather than the Neon serverless HTTP driver.",
        "evidence": "The Neon guide's current answer is that \"with Vercel Fluid, Neon recommends a normal Postgres TCP connection using `pg.Pool` (for example, with `node-postgres`), rather than `@neondatabase/serverless`\", described as the fastest option once established, with `@neondatabase/serverless` retained for classic serverless compute where connections cannot be reused. The same guide supplies `DATABASE_URL` directly to a `pg.Pool`. Note this guidance is recent: earlier tutorials default to the serverless driver, so it is worth re-checking at implementation time.",
        "source": "https://neon.com/docs/guides/vercel-connection-methods",
        "confidence": 74,
        "affects": "stack.choice (pg rather than @neondatabase/serverless), the `src/db.js` module, the pooled-versus-direct connection-string invariant"
      },
      {
        "claim": "Neon publishes both a pooled and a direct connection string, and the pooled one is the one the app should use; the direct one is for migrations.",
        "evidence": "Neon's own Vercel guidance and the PlanetScale-hosted copy of Neon's driver documentation both describe the pooled endpoint (the `-pooler` host) as the one for the application runtime and the direct endpoint for migrations, `psql` and long-running jobs; using a non-pooled string in serverless environments is a commonly reported cause of \"connection pool exhausted\".",
        "source": "https://neon.com/docs/guides/vercel-connection-methods and https://planetscale.com/docs/postgres/connecting/neon-serverless-driver",
        "confidence": 78,
        "affects": "src/db.js, the deploy section's environment variables, TR-1"
      },
